title: GH#36000: fix(pulse): make draft checkpoint cooldown take effect across cycles (GH#36000)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36000 (t18795).

- Attribute checkpoint continuation verdicts to the issue for production log filtering.
- Never cool transient continuation launch failures.
- Extend quiet, unassigned checkpoint records to six hours, preserving revision/label invalidation and base disable behavior.

Files: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`.
Reference: existing checkpoint negative-cache reader and candidate log filter.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: medium. Testing level: runtime-verified.

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` — PASS
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — PASS
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` — PASS
- `shellcheck` on all four changed scripts — PASS
- `git diff --check` — PASS

The pre-push hook reports `bun run typecheck` cannot start because this runner has no installed TypeScript dev dependencies (`tsc: command not found`); the existing CI typecheck owns that unrelated check. This shell-only change does not alter Node/TypeScript files.

## Acceptance self-review

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Helper verdicts reach the issue-specific reader and record cooldown | Real attention emitter plus production LOGFILE reader; realistic no-stall and capability-release verdicts; issue-prefix and repo isolation |
| Quiet unassigned records survive base TTL | One-hour-old record remains filtered with default six-hour quiet TTL |
| Recent or assigned records keep base expiry | 14399/14400-second write-time horizon boundary and assigned snapshot coverage |
| Disable and invalidation preserved | Base zero, quiet zero, revision/label edits, label-order invariance, invalid-setting fallback, one-day cap |
| Transient launch windows never cool | Launch-failure log windows and preserved older PR-fingerprinted block |
| Other reasons unchanged | Existing runner-capability and PR-fingerprint paths remain independent; only checkpoint-cooldown branch selects quiet TTL |

No deployment or release was authorized. After deployment, the operational owner can verify checkpoint-skip log entries across cycles and reduced failed candidate-stage time; this PR does not claim those production metrics.

title: GH#36005: fix: close stale-reset never-ready claims and ready attempt rebinds in checkpoint history
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36005.

A preserved draft checkpoint could not get approved after later dispatch episodes had fully released. `approval-template` returned `intervening coordination is not fully released`. A read-only replay found two framework causes:

1. **Producer bug (manual dispatch).** `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` never allocated an attempt ID. Its prelaunch lease used whatever `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_ID` the caller had, and the worker argv left the ID out. Since GH#35295 the worker runs in a managed `systemd-run --user` unit, which doesn't inherit the caller's environment, so the worker created a fresh ID before its ready lease. Pulse dispatch was never affected: `_dlw_begin_prelaunch` passes one ID in argv.
   - Fix: allocate one `attempt:` ID per dispatch (`_dsi_ensure_attempt_id`), pass it to the prelaunch transition and in the worker argv, and drop any inherited `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_STARTED_AT`.
2. **History rejected two legitimate closures** (`pr_checkpoint_history.py`):
   - A claim that never reached ready, released by its owner's stale recovery (`reason=stale_assignment_reset`). This now closes as `outcome: stale_reset_before_ready`, under every `blocked_before_ready` guard plus a mandatory device match with the claim.
   - Prelaunch→ready attempt rotation (historical records from bug 1). History now accepts exactly one rebind at the first ready lease. It must come before any launch or release, on the claim's lease token, session and device. Later leases, launches and releases must match the rebound attempt.

Both remain explicit `released_successors` entries that a new approval must acknowledge; neither grants continuation by itself.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: attempt allocation and propagation.
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`: `close_stale_reset_before_ready`, `lease_attempt_accepted`, claim device recorded in episode state (not emitted).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py`: positive and fail-closed cases (wrong or missing device, live renewal, ready, launch, foreign actor, edit, unbound attempt; rebind after launch, second rebind, foreign device, terminal or release naming the prelaunch attempt, prelaunch-phase rebind, unprefixed ID).
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: documents both closures.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py`: 13 tests OK (4 new).
- `test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py` (19 OK), `test-pr-checkpoint-private-member.py` (5 OK), `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` (120 passed), `test-dispatch-single-issue-prelaunch.sh` and `test-dispatch-single-issue-tracking.sh` pass.
- `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: 97/98. The one failure ("fresh runner capabilities block … checkpoint resume") reproduces identically on unmodified `main` scripts (managed lifetime evidence unavailable on macOS). It predates this PR and is unrelated.
- ShellCheck clean. Pre-commit ratchets pass.
- Read-only replay of the observed private checkpoint history (5 intervening episodes):
  - Unmodified code: `released_successor_history` returns `None`.
  - With this branch: the stale-reset episode and all three rotated-attempt episodes close.
  - With this branch plus #35513's unprefixed-ID normalisation (simulated in a temporary copy): all 5 episodes reconstruct.

## Relationship to #35513

The remaining episode in the observed history uses an unprefixed legacy attempt ID, which #35513 normalises. #35513 is based on an older `main` (`events()` signature differs) and will need a rebase. This PR does not depend on it.

title: GH#35968: detect alternating and non-progressing tool-call loops in continuation guard
body:
## Summary

Replaces the single previous-failure fingerprint with a bounded per-session window (new session-continuation-loops.mjs). Detects cycles of period 1-4: failing cycles repeated threshold times save the existing recovery checkpoint and correction (named by tool cycle); all-success cycles repeated threshold+2 times with identical output only steer, never checkpoint, so they cannot block completion. Only progress (a new edit fingerprint, or a TodoWrite content/status change) resets the window; plain successes no longer clear it. aidevops_bounded_operation status/output polling is exempt. Documented in reference/session.md. The Critical risk classification comes from the word session in the module names; no auth/login session code is touched.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-guard.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-loops.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-continuation-checkpoint-helper.mjs, .agents/reference/session.md

## Decisions

Success-only cycles require identical output and two extra repetitions to avoid false positives on polling with changing output, and they steer only. Signals are deduplicated per rotation-independent cycle signature until progress resets the window.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: drove the production guard through the same beforeTool/afterTool calls quality-hooks.mjs makes, with OpenCode-shaped bash outputs (metadata.exit 1). Before (main): 20 alternating A/B failures produced 0 replans. After: replan fires once at call 6 and appends the recovery correction to the tool output. node tests/test-session-continuation-checkpoint-helper.mjs passes new cases (identical failures at 3, A/B failures once at 6, fail/success alternation, identical success A/B at 10 with no checkpoint and no completion block, changing-output polling, reads+new edits, edit/todo resets, re-applied edits, bounded-operation polling). Full plugin suite npm --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops test exit 0; linters-local.sh --changed passes.

Resolves #35968

title: t18798: fix(plugin): stop denying all compound shell commands in every session (v3.39.87 regression)
body:
## Summary

f26477fca (GH#35978) moved the opaque-shell and interpreter -c denials in assertShellRead above the bound-session / empty-roots exemption. assertPrivateProcessingRead runs on every tool call, so since v3.39.87 every session (including sessions with no local-only roots) has every pipe, &&, ;, $VAR, glob and sh -c command denied with unclassifiable_shell_read. Headless workers stop at their first compound command and are released as permission_required, which waits for a maintainer retry. This keeps GH#35978's protections (literal operands are still canonically resolved before any exemption) and scopes the fail-closed denial: in bound or unclassified sessions, opaque text and -c scripts are denied only when they name a protected operator-config file (case-insensitive). Classified unbound sessions keep the strict literal-reader path.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/private-processing-policy.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-private-processing-policy.mjs, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18798-brief.md

## Decisions

Opaque shell text cannot be classified exactly; denying all of it in every session breaks normal operation. Matching protected config basenames in opaque text keeps the GH#35978 alias protection with negligible false positives. Classified unbound sessions are unchanged.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Probe against the deployed v3.39.87 module with no roots and an unbound session: `git status && git log -1 | head -5` and `sh -c 'git status'` were denied (unclassifiable_shell_read), matching the worker blocker. With this change both are allowed, and `cat local-only-roots.json | wc` is still denied. test-private-processing-policy.mjs: 9/9 pass, including every GH#35978 alias, symlink and interpreter assertion and a new GH#36017 regression test. Full plugin suite (node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/) exits 0.

Resolves #36017

title: GH#36019: t18799 fix(pulse): continue open worker drafts after draft-checkpoint, clean and completed releases
body:
## Summary

Open worker drafts were held silently after worker_draft_checkpoint, clean and worker_complete releases: dispatch-stalled ignored those reasons, blocked-attention only covered clean/worker_complete, and closing-linked drafts were projected status:blocked so the continuation target fence rejected them. title: t18800: fix(pulse): restore stranded worker draft checkpoints
body:
## Summary

Runners before v3.39.89 projected `status:blocked` after a `clean`/`worker_complete` release while the worker's draft PR stayed open. The dispatch candidate filter skips `status:blocked` and the stale-blocked sweep resolves only dependency blocks, so those drafts were never continued, merged or surfaced. GH#36019 fixed the projection; this PR recovers issues already stranded (and any an un-updated runner strands). Live examples: #35977 (PR #35984), #35918 (PR #35928), #35592 (PR #35598).

`pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh` runs as a pass on the per-repo stale-blocked cadence with its own stamp (`draft-checkpoint-unblock-complete`). It restores `status:available` (releasing only the runner's assignment) only when trusted evidence proves the block was that projection:

- open `auto-dispatch` issue whose only status is `status:blocked`, with no protective label;
- exactly one open `origin:worker` draft closing it, targeting the repository default branch (GitHub honours closing keywords only there);
- newest trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED` is unedited, posted by the runner it names, with a continuable reason (not `blocked`, policy timeouts or `worker_ownership_lost`), and no later claim, dispatch or non-terminal lease (the attempt's own terminal lease is ignored, GH#33839);
- newest `labeled status:blocked` event is that runner's within the release window (−60 s/+600 s); a later maintainer re-block wins;
- assignees are only that runner; no audit marker for that release; under the per-PR cap (3).

One audit comment per restore and one `draft-checkpoint-unblock:` Pulse log line per decision, including the failing stage for unreadable listings, comments or timelines. Pulse then routes the draft through the existing `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` → `dispatch-stalled` exact-head continuation or attention path. Drafts are never closed.

## History

The worker commit `2f3b7953ee` (dispatched for #36028) is preserved. An interactive session implemented the same brief in parallel (its claim was skipped while REST core was exhausted) and continued this branch with a merge (`9c5edb359b`). Review of the worker version found two defects, both verified:

1. Its ownership fence took the newest coordination event of any kind, so a release followed by the attempt's own `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal` (common: #35977 18:58:19→18:58:42; #36028 03:47:43→03:47:57) was silently skipped.
2. It passed the paginated timeline with `jq --argjson`; #35592's timeline is 149,244 bytes, above Linux's 131,072-byte per-argument limit, so on Linux runners that issue would fail the whole pass every cycle.

The resolution keeps the interactive module (stdin-piped evidence, full pagination, per-issue failure isolation, `auto-dispatch` requirement) and adopts the worker's unedited-release and poster-equals-runner checks, its reason-set sync check and its real cadence-stamp tests. CodeRabbit's stage-logging finding was applied (`5a12c506c9`), and the worker then added the default-branch target guard (`29d90e899d`). The claim gap that allowed the parallel run is tracked as #36036.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh (new), .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh (new), .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh (source module), .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh (pass + stamp via `_pulse_stale_blocked_optional_pass`), .agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md, TODO.md (t18800 entry; t18801 follow-up backlog entry)

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium — new label writes are gated on correlated trusted release and label-timeline evidence; every unreadable or ambiguous read means no write.
- **Verification:** `test-pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh` 57/57 at `29d90e899d` (including the large-timeline, terminal-lease, default-branch and stage-logging regressions and real cadence stamps). Sibling suites pass: `test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`, `test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh`, `test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`. ShellCheck clean; `complexity-regression-helper.sh` bash32-compat/nesting-depth/file-size/function-complexity: 0 new. Live read-only dry run against marcusquinn/aidevops (writes stubbed, labels confirmed unchanged afterwards): selects exactly #35977, #35918 and #35592 and none of the other 11 blocked issues.

Resolves #36028

body:
## Summary

Resolves #36032.

- Preserve termination-cause reporting and per-operation TERM grace already merged in #35835 (0937ed7f5).
- Expose the existing 900-second default and 24-hour clamp, effective budget receipt, plugin/session/host lifetime limits, progress protocol, and 0.5-second default TERM grace in the native tool description.
- Document that the bounded manager/supervisor has no separate two-hour or idle timeout.
- Add one focused case to the existing lifecycle suite using its injected manager clock/timer and real supervisor path.

## Files and reference pattern

Files: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs`, `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md`. Reference pattern: existing tool conversion, injected manager clock/timer options, and termination cases. Canonical Files Scope was persisted before edits. No process containment, timeout policy, credentials or security controls changed.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime-verified on pushed head `3f102cb655046fce0c62ba46cb1aa786708e853a`, Node v22.23.3 (declared engine >=20).

Passed:

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs
git diff --check
```

32/32 tests passed, 49.1 seconds. The new test verifies both 86,400-second and oversized requests produce an 86,400,000-ms timer/receipt; after advancing only the manager clock to 7,216 seconds, status is still running with 79,184,000 ms remaining, no progress and no termination cause. The command then succeeds through the real supervisor. This is NOT a real two-hour soak.

Also exercised the existing native tool with budget_seconds=14400, kill_grace_seconds=60 and a Bash TERM trap that sleeps 30 seconds. After observing handler-ready, cancelled it: terminal state cancelled, termination_cause=cancel, process_exit=0, process_signal=null; captured output contains TERM received followed by cleaned. This runtime check exercises the already-deployed #35835 grace implementation, not a newly changed supervisor.

Local static-tool availability: markdownlint-cli2, biome and qlty are not on PATH. Existing code-quality.yml markdownlint/biome jobs and Qlty cover these checks. Unchanged pre-push hooks passed and explicitly deferred typecheck to CI because local tsc dependencies are absent; no root typecheck pass is claimed.

## Acceptance and review

Direct diff/self-review: only the tool description, six documentation lines and one focused existing-suite case changed; no lifecycle implementation was rewritten.

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit effective budget and maximum | Tool/reference describe existing 24-hour clamp; regression verifies exact timer/receipt |
| Overdue output/progress does not impose two-hour cutoff | Manager-clock regression at 7,216 seconds; supervisor/manager source has only budget/lifecycle termination paths |
| Configurable TERM grace | Existing #35835 implementation; real 30-second trap completed within 60-second grace |
| Cause in status | Existing distinct-cause regressions pass; native cancellation receipt reports cancel |
| Historical sender | Unknown; no historical attribution or real two-hour soak claimed |

The budget is not a durable scheduler guarantee. Plugin reload/disposal, deleted sessions, host shutdown or external signals can still stop operations. Restart OpenCode after deployment to load the updated tool description.
